content.description: Cross-section diagram of valve head showing margin measurement location

content.text: Minimum margin: Intake 0.5 mm (0.020 in.) Exhaust 1.0 mm (0.039 in.)
If the valve head margin is less than specified, replace the valve.

content.description: Illustration showing valve stem tip being checked and ground on a grinding wheel

content.text: (c) Check the surface of the valve stem tip for wear.
Standard overall length: Intake 107.5 mm (4.232 in.) Exhaust 109.7 mm (4.319 in.)
If the valve stem tip is worn, resurface the tip with a grinder or replace the valve.
CAUTION: Do not grind more than 0.5 mm (0.020 in.).

items: (a) Using a 45° carbide cutter, resurface the valve seats. Remove only enough metal to clean the seats.

(b) Check the valve seating position. Apply a thin coat of prussian blue (or white lead) to the valve face. Install the valve. While applying light pressure to the valve, rotate the valve against the seat.

content.description: Hand illustration showing valve being rotated against seat with marking compound
Illustration showing inspection of valve face and seat with blue marking

content.text: (c) Check the valve face and seat for the following:

items: • If blue appears 360° around the face, the valve is concentric. If not, replace the valve.
• If blue appears 360° around the valve seat, the guide and seat are concentric. If not, resurface the seat.

content.description: Technical diagram showing valve seat contact angles: 60° (IN), 67.5° (EX) at top, 30° 45° at middle positions, with 1.2-1.6 mm width specification

items: • Check that the seat contact is on the middle of the valve face with the following width: 1.2 — 1.6 mm (0.047 — 0.063 in.)

content.text: If seating is too high on the valve face, use 30° and 45° cutters to correct the seat.
If seating is too low on the valve face, use 60° (IN) or 67.5° (EX) and 45° cutters to correct the seat.
